title: Extracellular PROX1 transfer restrains Müller glia reprogramming
observed: Blocking extracellular PROX1 transfer promoted Müller glia reprogramming, retinal neuron generation and delayed visual decline in a mouse model.
notShown: Safe or effective retinal regeneration in living humans; durable restoration of normal vision.
safety: PROX1 is important in other tissues; long-term and cell-specific safety remain unresolved.
conflict: Some authors disclosed interests related to Celliaz.

title: PROX1 localization in degenerating human retinal tissue
observed: Accumulation of PROX1 was reported in Müller glia in degenerating human retinal donor tissue.
notShown: That PROX1 inhibition produces new working retinal neurons or restores vision in patients.
safety: Protein localization is mechanistic context, not an intervention or clinical result.
conflict: See source publication for full disclosures.

title: ASCL1 plus chromatin modulation produces retinal neuron-like cells
observed: ASCL1 expression with histone deacetylase inhibition generated neuronal-feature cells with light-responsive properties in adult mice.
notShown: Normal vision restored in humans or a proven safe clinical treatment.
safety: Forced cell-state changes warrant careful evaluation of cell identity and long-term stability.

title: Dual PTEN and SOCS3 deletion enhances injured optic-nerve axon growth
observed: Cell-specific removal of both inhibitory proteins supported more sustained axon regrowth than either manipulation alone.
notShown: Full functional restoration of the human optic nerve or an approved intervention.
safety: PTEN is a major tumor suppressor; systemic deletion would not be a safe clinical strategy.

title: NG101 targeting Nogo-A after cervical spinal cord injury
observed: The antibody treatment did not produce a statistically significant improvement on the prespecified primary upper-extremity motor score for the overall trial population.
notShown: Clinical efficacy in the trial population or regrowth of severed spinal pathways.
safety: Exploratory subgroup signals require independent prospective confirmation.
source: Weidner et al., The Lancet Neurology (2025)
conflict: Consult published trial report for sponsor and investigator disclosures.

title: YAP–EN1 signaling changes mouse skin healing and scarring
observed: Inhibiting fibroblast YAP or EN1 activation promoted wound healing with regenerative features, including skin appendages, in mice.
notShown: A validated scar-free wound therapy for people.
safety: YAP affects growth and has different roles in distinct tissues; blanket inhibition is not supported.

title: Inherited MSTN loss of function increases human muscle mass
observed: An inherited myostatin loss-of-function variant was associated with pronounced muscle hypertrophy in one child.
notShown: Effective muscle regeneration, general health benefits, or an approved myostatin-blocking treatment.
safety: Increased muscle size does not automatically mean improved strength or tissue repair.

title: FGF2 and GSK3 modulation in cultured adult human retina
observed: Adult donor retinal cultures showed Müller glia proliferation and markers associated with neuronal lineage commitment after signaling interventions.
notShown: New functionally integrated neurons in living patients or restored human vision.
safety: Ex vivo markers are not clinical efficacy; findings require peer review and replication.
